channel.title: The Batch | DeepLearning.AI
channel.description: Weekly AI news for engineers, executives, and enthusiasts.

item.title: Leaders Lock Models Away: Could companies or governments shut down frontier AI development?
item.description: Fearful of their own discoveries, AI engineers at top companies warn that frontier models have improved too quickly to be properly guided, understood, or restrained.

item.title: AI Detectors Find the Devil’s Work: Writers, students, engineers face false accusations of using AI
item.description: Last month, the Haiti-born, Quebec-based author Thélyson Orélien won a prestigious literary prize for C’était ça ou mourir (It Was Either That or Die), his French-language novel about a teacher forced to flee Haiti’s gang violence.

item.title: AI Bites the Hand That Feeds It: Scientists, other users fear AI companies will train on or misuse sensitive data
item.description: Developers, scientists, and businesses feed AI tools their private code, unpublished research, and confidential files.

item.title: Dawn of the Agents: Will AI agents self-organize or lose control due to bad safety practices?
item.description: This year, AI agents escaped containment at several labs, conspired with each other online, and infiltrated other organizations’ systems.

item.title: How to Face Your AI Fears This Year: Introduction to a special Halloween 2026 edition of The Batch
item.description: Following our annual tradition, this special Halloween edition of The Batch treats leading AI fears.

item.title: Zombie Agents, Vampire Models, Witch Hunts, and the Mummy's Curse: AI Fears for Halloween 2026

item.title: How to read the top model leaderboard: Who pays the most for AI inference and context?
item.description: Unlimited OCR2 could be your new scanning model. Genie 4 worries traditional video game developers. OpenAI produces proofs of major science theorems. Post-training method dispenses with human-written datasets.

item.title: Anthropic’s public filing offers clues to its future: Kimi K3.1 Pro performs among top models overall
item.description: RSI’s MoE model has open weights, advances recursion. OpenAI Decisions API opens for general use. Claude Duet agent triages office tasks for paid users. AI radio show gains traction with U.S. Latinos.

item.title: A Single Decoder Turns Small Models into Action: TurboVLA turns to a throwback architecture to attend to language and vision
item.description: The vision-language-action architecture that increasingly drives robots relies on a large language model to combine visual observations with text instructions before an action decoder produces motor commands.

item.title: Nvidia Courts A New Partner: Reflection releases Beam, an open weight model from an independent U.S.-based lab
item.description: Reflection AI, a closely-watched, Nvidia-backed U.S. startup, announced its first model.

item.title: ChatGPT for Teens Gets a Report Card: OpenAI adds features for youths as studies doubt program's safety and educational impact
item.description: OpenAI announced that it would add college-planning and study tools to its under-18 experience.

item.title: Meta Releases Wonder, Opens Spark: All about Muse Wonder (API), Muse Wonder Full (subscription), and Muse Spark Open (weights available)
item.description: Meta marched all the way back to the AI frontier to offer a Muse model for everyone.
